title: Deoxylapachol inhibits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression via targeting FOXM1-mediated Wnt/beta-catenin pathway.
authors: Qi, Jingru; Wang, Lurong; Zhou, Yehan; Chen, Qian; Sun, Xin; Yu, Xiushi; Si, Daiyin; Ma, Ketao; Zhang, Qiang; Wang, Yanming
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物DEO通过靶向FOXM1抑制食管鳞癌，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白作用与肿瘤机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a significant global health challenge. Deoxylapachol (DEO) is a natural quinone compound from the Cichorium glandulosum Boiss. et Huet. However, the effects and potential mechanisms of DEO against ESCC remain unclear. PURPOSE: To investigate the effects and potential mechanisms of DEO against ESCC. METHODS: Bioinformatics analysis, Western blot, qRT-PCR, colony formation, EdU, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy and a xenograft mouse model were used in this study. RESULTS: DEO significantly suppressed ESCC cell migration and invasion while inducing ferroptosis and cytoplasmic alkalization, accompanied by elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Bioinformatics analysis identified FOXM1 as a core potential target of DEO and revealed the involvement of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway in its anti-ESCC mechanism. Molecular docking, MD simulations, and SPR analysis confirmed that DEO directly targets FOXM1. Moreover, FOXM1, MYBL2, and CDCA3 were found to be positively correlated and overexpressed in human ESCC tissues. DEO treatment markedly downregulated their expression, which was associated with the inhibition of malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, the inhibition of ESCC progression by DEO might be mediated through the targeting of FOXM1, concomitant downregulation of MYBL2 and CDCA3, and subsequent suppression of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, as validated by combined shFOXM1 and oeFOXM1 approaches. CONCLUSION: Our study is the first to demonstrate the potent anti-ESCC effects of DEO. The results indicate DEO may inhibit ESCC progression through targeting FOXM1-mediated Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, positioning DEO as a promising candidate for the development of novel ESCC therapeutics.
abstract_zh: 背景：食管鳞状细胞癌（ESCC）是全球重大健康挑战。脱氧拉帕醇（DEO）是从菊苣（Cichorium glandulosum Boiss. et Huet.）中提取的天然醌类化合物。然而，DEO对ESCC的作用及其潜在机制尚不清楚。目的：探讨DEO对ESCC的作用及其潜在机制。方法：本研究采用生物信息学分析、Western blot、qRT-PCR、集落形成、EdU、分子对接、分子动力学（MD）、表面等离子体共振（SPR）、免疫组织化学、透射电子显微镜及异种移植小鼠模型。结果：DEO显著抑制ESCC细胞迁移和侵袭，同时诱导铁死亡和细胞质碱化，并伴随活性氧（ROS）生成增加。生物信息学分析将FOXM1鉴定为DEO的核心潜在靶点，并揭示Wnt/β-catenin通路参与其抗ESCC机制。分子对接、MD模拟和SPR分析证实DEO直接靶向FOXM1。此外，FOXM1、MYBL2和CDCA3在人ESCC组织中呈正相关且过表达。DEO处理显著下调其表达，这与恶性表型的抑制相关。机制上，DEO抑制ESCC进展可能通过靶向FOXM1、伴随下调MYBL2和CDCA3，以及随后抑制Wnt/β-catenin通路介导，这通过结合shFOXM1和oeFOXM1方法得到验证。结论：本研究首次证明DEO具有强效抗ESCC作用。结果表明，DEO可能通过靶向FOXM1介导的Wnt/β-catenin通路抑制ESCC进展，使DEO成为开发新型ESCC治疗药物的有前景候选者。
